newsitem.title: CHINA: China share indices end down on faded HK rally.
newsitem.headline: China share indices end down on faded HK rally.

text.p: China's A and B share indices ended down on Wednesday as hopes of a rally before the Hong Kong handover faded, brokers said.
The markets are also concerned about the government's attitude towards the markets after the handover, they said.

The Shanghai B share index fell 1.487 points or 1.75 percent to 83.457 on volume of 14.195 million shares worth $8.461 million and the Shenzhen B index dipped 2.41 points or 1.64 percent to 144.53 on turnover of HK$77 million.

Brokers in Shanghai said Pudong shares saw a correction today on institutional profit-taking due to uncertainties about the government's attitude toward the market after the handover of Hong Kong at midnight on June 30.
"Heavy institutional selling in Pudong shares pushed the index down," said one broker.
"With the approach of the Hong Kong handover, institutions cannot find any new excuse to boost buying interest, and have begun to liquidate their positions," another broker said.
"The (Shenzhen) B share market's recent poor performance dampened investor confidence," the China Guotai analyst said.
"I am not optimistic about the (Shenzhen) B share market's performance later this week," an analyst at Shenzhen J&A Securities said.
In Shenzhen, concerns that the forthcoming listing of a number of new issues will suck funds away from the existing shares also triggered selling today, brokers said.
"People cut their positions ahead of a flood of new listings and a long holiday," a Shenzhen broker at China Guotai Securities said.

In term of B shares, China's giant Bengang Steel Plates Co Ltd has completed its initial public offering (IPO) of 460 million B shares for listing in Shenzhen in early July. Bengang raised about one billion yuan from the IPO.
Seven companies will list a combined 340 million A shares in Shenzhen on Thursday, a record for one day on the south China bourse, brokers said.
In addition, three companies will go public in the city's A share market on Friday.
Shanghai Dazhong Taxi was the biggest loser in Shanghai on institutional profit-taking, slipping $0.046 or 4.97 percent to $0.878 on volume of 1.0 million shares.
Pudong shares Shanghai Jinqiao Export Processing Zone Development also fell sharply on institutional selling to unwind positions, down $0.036 or 4.12 percent to $0.836 on volume of 896,000 shares.
Jiangling Motors was the biggest loser on the Shenzhen B share market, tumbling HK$0.27 or 7.83 percent to HK$3.18.

The Shanghai A index dipped 6.147 points or 0.45 percent to 1,356.720 points on volume of 420.4 million shares worth 6.1 billion yuan. The SSE30 blue chip index ended down 16.980 points or 0.41 percent to 4,136.621 points.
The Shenzhen domestic A share index slipped 0.38 points or 0.08 percent to 463.21 on turnover of 9.2 billion yuan.
